analysis: Integration of four unit analyses. The PR is docs/changelog, a LaunchAgent.swift change and tests. LaunchAgent.kickstartInPlace (provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Service/LaunchAgent.swift, about lines 196-222) now returns Bool. kickstartIfLoaded passes reloadIfMissing=false, which is the watchdog path. When launchctl reports the service is gone (exit 113, '3:' or 'could not find service'), it now returns false instead of true. With reloadIfMissing=true it reloads via loadService and returns true. This strengthens the property that the watchdog never resurrects a user-stopped or uninstalled provider (TB-003, T-043). It adds no privilege, no network surface and no change to attestation, encryption, key handling or serving authorization (TB-011, A-016). The restart() caller discards the result via @discardableResult. The new tests (LaunchAgentLifecycleTests.swift, about lines 466 and 496-670) use task-local launchctl seams and a temp home, so they add no production surface. They assert no enable/bootstrap, an unchanged plist and a byte-identical restored guard file. The stderr.contains("3:") heuristic is loose, but it was already in the code and only shifts a return-false versus throw outcome, not authorization. Not verified, because the files were not supplied: WatchdogRecoveryService.recoverDownProvider and KVBackendCrashLoopGuard, meaning how they handle the false return, whether the guard rollback restores the exact prior bytes, and the file permissions, atomicity and races involved. T-043's full text was oversized and not seen. No findings qualify. The T-043 availability/crash-loop masking concern is a residual question, not a demonstrated regression.
